audit.why: A player reading the header sees HARD and plays scared in a lane the rest of the page tells them to bully. The rating, the tone colour and both difficulty strings already agree with the data.
audit.corrected: diff HARD -> FAV. No prose needed to move with it because the prose already reads 'Favoured matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 and Level 6 were on the wrong side of the mirror, and 2+ items disagreed with the packet.
audit.why: The mirror moved rows 1 and 4 to Illaoi and raised her row-4 rating to 6/10, so my side must read Illaoi with 4/10 there. My own whys[4] already says 'at 6 she's scariest', so row 4 was contradicting its own text. Row 6 was marked Illaoi while whys[6] says 'you reclaim it' and the packet chart says Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Neeko's spike while the same page explains that ulting inside her tentacle field hands her a free Spirit-slam.
audit.why: Pop Blossom has a preparation before the leap and Illaoi's whole kit answers a stationary commit. The real Neeko spike in this matchup is first item, when Q clears from outside tentacle range — which the page already says.
audit.corrected: Row 4 moved to Illaoi; the spike text was already honest and is left as written.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells the player to dodge Test of Spirit with 'Shapesplitter (W) clone + invis'. Neeko has no invisibility.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text is a third-attack proc plus a directional clone. The mirror made the same correction from Illaoi's side. Against Illaoi the clone alone is the tool — it is what her E can be baited onto.

audit.whatIsWrong: Harsh Lesson's auto-attack reset was never named as the burst tell.
audit.why: _missing flags autoreset-burst-tell. It is a 4-second leap to her target that also makes nearby tentacles swing — the shortest cooldown in her kit and the actual opener of every trade. The hop is the cue to leave, not the moment she starts walking.
audit.corrected: Written into mid with its 4s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her sustain is mentioned in early ('her sustain heals the poke back') without ever saying where it comes from or what answers it.
audit.why: _missing flags needs-antiheal. Riot's passive text is explicit: tentacles heal Illaoi when they damage a champion. Grievous Wounds timing is what makes poke stick in a lane whose whole plan is poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit is the matchup's focus and its cooldown appears nowhere; dosFull[2].d calls it 'the fifteen-second invitation', which is close but not a rank value.
audit.why: It is 16/15/14/13/12s. At rank 1 that is a genuinely long window and the reason the lane is winnable at all.
audit.corrected: 16s written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and mid.

edits.before: Even-ish at 2: your second Q point pokes but she gets her first tentacles down, so trading edges toward a coin-flip if you over-step.
edits.after: She edges 2: your second Q point still pokes, but her first tentacles are down and every one that connects heals her straight back off the passive.

edits.before: Level 1 you actually own it: chuck Blooming Burst (Q) at Illaoi over the minions and the re-bloom chips her while her only answer is to step onto her own tentacles or eat it. Through Levels 2-3 keep poking from max range and NEVER throw Tangle-Barbs (E) when you're standing in her tentacle field, because rooting yourself there means every tentacle slams you and her Test of Spirit (E) yanks your spirit. Last-hit at Q's edge and respect that her sustain heals the poke back if you let her free-farm on top of her tentacles.
edits.after: Level 1 you actually own it: chuck Blooming Burst (Q) at Illaoi over the minions and the re-bloom chips her while her only answer is to step onto her own tentacles or eat it. Through Levels 2-3 keep poking from max range and NEVER throw Tangle-Barbs (E) while standing in her tentacle field, because rooting yourself there means every tentacle slams you and Test of Spirit yanks your spirit. Last-hit at Q's edge and get Grievous Wounds early — every tentacle that lands on a champion heals her, which erases a lane of poke.

edits.before: This is where she's scariest, not you — at 6 her tentacle field plus a landed Test of Spirit (E) turns one bad step into a full Spirit-slam combo that out-bursts your single rotation. Don't channel Pop Blossom (R) anywhere near 3+ live tentacles; bait her E first with a Shapesplitter (W) clone, let her commit, then re-engage on her cooldown. Your real win condition here isn't the 1v1 brawl on her terms — it's clearing the wave with Q from range and roaming while she's stuck shoving with no mobility.
edits.after: This is where she's scariest, not you — at 6 her tentacle field plus a landed Test of Spirit (E) turns one bad step into a full Spirit-slam that out-bursts your single rotation. Don't wind up Pop Blossom (R) near 3+ live tentacles; bait her E with a Shapesplitter (W) clone, then re-engage inside its 16 seconds. Harsh Lesson is a 4s leap that resets her auto — that hop is your cue to step back. Your win condition isn't the brawl on her terms; it's clearing with Q from range and roaming while she's stuck shoving.

notes: Not asserted, deliberately: the kit file's derived flags put 'grounding' and 'untargetable' on Leap of Faith, and _missing raises both as interactions (deny Pop Blossom's dash, dodge your burst). Riot's own description of Leap of Faith is only 'smashes her idol into the ground, dealing physical damage to nearby enemies. A Tentacle spawns for each enemy champion hit' — no grounding, no untargetability. Per the rule that the description beats a misfiring flag, I wrote neither onto the page. If the user confirms Leap of Faith grounds, it belongs in spikes[1] and dontsFull, because it would mean her ult hard-denies Pop Blossom's leap. Second item: row 1 is a genuine mirror-vs-packet conflict — the mirror moved it to Illaoi, my packet chart says Skill. I followed the mirror to avoid an overwrite, and rewrote whys[1] so the text no longer says 'even-ish' on a row the chart gives to her. Also, both Illaoi's and Neeko's pronouns are mixed on the full layer ('force Illaoi to play scared of every minion in his wave'), which is a mechanical find/replace rather than per-string edits.
